URL: https://www.iranintl.com/en/202611199940
Iran International, 19-20 November 2026

The three leaders are scheduled to meet Thursday afternoon in Shenzhen, China, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.

Speaking to Fox News senior White House correspondent Jacqui Heinrich in Shenzhen, Trump said: “We don't need any help. We've defeated their navy. We've defeated their air force. We've defeated their anti-aircraft.”

“I'm not going to go in asking for help,” he said, adding that the United States had total control of the Strait of Hormuz.

Earlier this week, Trump said he planned to discuss Iran, the war in Ukraine, nuclear arms control and trade with Xi and Putin. The precise agenda remains unclear.

The diplomatic gathering also comes amid differences between Washington, Beijing and Moscow over trade and international security. Xi criticized trade protectionism and called for open trade, while Putin said Western sanctions imposed on Russia over the war in Ukraine had backfired.

Trump also told Fox News that a preliminary agreement with Iran reached in Islamabad had been “a waste of time,” while pledging to bring the war to an end soon.

“I want a deal that can be lasting,” he said. “I'm going to finish it off — soon. One way or the other, we'll finish it off.”

He praised the US naval blockade of Iran as Washington's most effective measure and said the preliminary understanding had allowed the administration to assess Tehran's approach to negotiations.

The comments came amid reports that Washington was considering renewed military action against Iran. The New York Times reported Wednesday that Trump was weighing another round of extensive strikes, although no decision had been made.

Trump warns of Iran's chemical, biological weapons

Trump also said there were indications Iran was exploring chemical and biological weapons following US efforts to curb its nuclear program.

“There is an indication that Iran is looking at gas, is looking at bio, because we've shut them out with the nuclear,” he told Fox News.

Asked about reports of a possible Iranian plot to detonate a radioactive dirty bomb in Washington, Trump warned of retaliation.

“If it does happen, we wipe them out,” he said.

CNN reported Monday, citing seven US officials, that intelligence indicated Iran was developing plans to potentially target senior Trump administration officials in Washington with a radioactive dirty bomb or chemical weapon.

US officials differed over whether Iran had the capability or intention to carry out such an attack, according to CNN.

The New York Times also reported Wednesday that US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's relocation to a military base was linked to Israeli intelligence about an Iranian plot to use chemical agents against senior American officials, citing a person briefed on the intelligence.

"])•••$RC("B:5","S:5")More StoriesBessent's relocation linked to Iran chemical threat – NYTNov 19, 2026, 01:42 GMT+0Listen to this article100%US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent speaks during the National Committee on US-China Relations 60th Anniversary Gala Dinner in New York City, US, November 10, 2026. REUTERSUS Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's relocation to a military base was linked to Israeli intelligence about an alleged Iranian plot to use chemical agents against senior American officials, The New York Times reported Wednesday, citing a person briefed on the intelligence.

Bessent relocated from his Washington-area home to a military base earlier this month following threats attributed to Iran. In a Friday interview with CNBC, he said he had followed Secret Service instructions and would not be intimidated by the threats.

The Treasury secretary has spearheaded Washington's economic pressure campaign against Iran, including Operation Economic Outcast, launched in August to tighten sanctions and financial restrictions and pressure Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

The reported threat comes amid broader US intelligence concerns about possible Iranian attacks against senior American officials.

US officials differed over whether Iran had the capability or intention to carry out such an attack.

President Donald Trump said Tuesday that Washington was examining the intelligence and warned Iran of severe consequences if it carried out an attack.

“Well, if there is, they will pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before,” Trump told reporters in Manila when asked whether an attack was imminent.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday that he did not believe Washington faced an imminent threat.

“I don't think there is any imminent threat,” Rubio told reporters, adding that US authorities remained alert to potential dangers.

Iran's Foreign Ministry rejected the allegations as baseless. The White House said it was monitoring potential threats but had identified no credible threat to the US homeland at that time.

Israeli officials have also warned that Iran could equip drones with chemical or biological weapons to attack Israel or neighboring countries, according to the Times.

US intelligence officials have identified indications of Iranian efforts to strengthen chemical and biological weapons capabilities, the newspaper reported. However, the Times said US intelligence officials largely assessed that Iran was developing those capabilities as a deterrent against major US or Israeli attacks, rather than for preemptive use.

US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told a congressional hearing Wednesday that threats from Iran against Americans at home and abroad had increased substantially, although he declined to discuss specific intelligence about the reported Washington attack plot.

Listen to this article100%FILE PHOTO: Iranian missiles are displayed at the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Aerospace Force Museum in Tehran, Iran, November 12, 2025.US officials warned Wednesday of Iranian threats against Americans and sanctioned Tehran-linked networks, while Iranian officials threatened regional oil infrastructure, missile strikes and revenge for Ali Khamenei's killing.

In written testimony submitted to the House Homeland Security Committee, FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia accused Iran of espionage, cyber operations and plots against American officials and dissidents, citing 18 Iran-related counterintelligence and espionage arrests since President Donald Trump returned to office.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin warned that Iranian cyber operatives increasingly targeted US transportation, healthcare, water, energy and financial services.

Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton also described a substantial increase in threats from Iran, particularly plots targeting Americans at home and abroad.

Washington's response extended to Iran's regional financial networks, with the Treasury Department sanctioning a Hezbollah-linked charity and a gold-and-cash smuggling network in Lebanon and Turkey.

The department said the network transferred funds from the Revolutionary Guards' Quds Force to Lebanon on Hezbollah's behalf, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pledged continued action against Tehran's financing operations.

Iranian officials warn of retaliation and wider attacks

In Tehran, officials issued a series of threats of their own. The Intelligence Ministry said it was awaiting an opportunity to avenge the killing of former Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and other Iranian officials, while Ahmadreza Pourkhaghan, head of the armed forces' judicial organization, called for identifying and targeting US and Israeli military bases in the region.

The warnings extended to Iran's missile capabilities. Deputy Basij chief Ghasem Ghoreishi said Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei had ordered the armed forces to extend their missile range, while Army Chief Amir Hatami warned of a stronger response to “adversaries' mistakes.”

Hassan Ghashghavi, spokesman for parliament's national security committee, went further, saying: “Today, the enemy does not know on which continent the Islamic Republic’s missiles will land.” He also dismissed the prospect of concessions to Washington.

Earlier Wednesday, the US military warned that vessels receiving Iranian cargo through ship-to-ship transfers could face seizure or other enforcement action under Washington's naval blockade.

Deputy Parliament Speaker Hamidreza Haji Babaei turned his attention to regional energy infrastructure, calling for attacks on oil pipelines and ship-to-ship transfers bypassing the Strait of Hormuz.

He argued that other countries should be prevented from exporting oil while Iran's exports remained blocked and threatened energy facilities in countries allowing attacks on Iran from their territory.

Wednesday's developments reflected an increasingly confrontational exchange, with Washington targeting Iranian security and financial networks while Tehran threatened to expand the geographic reach and economic consequences of any renewed conflict.

REUTERSIraq's army was awaiting orders Wednesday to take control of a stronghold of Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah south of Baghdad, as reports emerged that IRGC Quds Force commander Esmail Qaani had met Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi to help defuse the escalating standoff.
